name: Patsy Cline
hook: A Virginia singer whose producer gave her strings and backing choirs to sell country to pop listeners, and whose biggest record was a jazz-chorded song by an unknown writer called Willie Nelson.
blurb: Patsy Cline was born Virginia Patterson Hensley in Winchester, Virginia, on 8 September 1932. Her family was poor and she worked in a chicken factory as a girl. She first sang on local radio, WINC, at 15. Her first record deal, with 4 Star in 1954, gave the label most of the money and her less than three per cent in royalties. She moved to Nashville in 1958, joined the Grand Ole Opry, and in 1960 signed to Decca, where the producer Owen Bradley surrounded her with smooth backing singers (the Jordanaires), Floyd Cramer's piano and strings, a style called the Nashville sound. It made her one of the first country singers to have hits on the pop charts too. 'Crazy' (recorded August and September 1961) was written by Willie Nelson, then an unknown songwriter, whose song she had at first refused to record. He taught it to her himself in her living room, singing behind the beat, and Bradley asked her to sing it her own way. By 1996 it was the most played song on American jukeboxes. She died in a plane crash near Camden, Tennessee, on 5 March 1963, aged 30, with Cowboy Copas, Hawkshaw Hawkins and her manager Randy Hughes. In 1973 she became the first woman in the Country Music Hall of Fame.
